Feedback on "Greg" Garmin coach experience

I have been running on an off for the better part of the last decade. I have had no goal in mind, no race, and was running by myself. Basically trying to be active only. I recently had my watch die on me (TicWatch Pro 5) and I switched to a Garmin one (Instinct 3 Solar). To make a long story short, I was browsing the app on my phone and after a few clicks I "registered" myself with "Coach Greg" and the goal of finishing a half marathon by late October. My previous longest run was 10 miles a couple of months ago. I've had periods where I did a 10k a week. The app started with a "benchmark run" where I was supposed to run for a short distance without pushing it. So I ran like a grandma around the block and the watch was happy. Then the training started: - Friday: benchmark - Monday: stride run. 5min warmup + strides + 5min cool down. That was nice, I had never done strides. - Wednesday: 30 min run + optional 10 min (after 5min warmup / before 5 min cooldown). That was also nice. - Friday: 10 min "easy run" + optional 10 min (5wu/5cd). That was way too easy - Monday: 10 min "easy run" + optional 10 min (5/5). Again way too easy - Wednesday: 10 min "easy run" (tomorrow) - Friday: stride (15m warmup, 10 strides, 15 min cool down) That Monday was yesterday. Both on Friday and yesterday I actually ran 40 minutes (with 5 warmup / 5 cooldown) because this is more what I'm used to. Did I screw up everything by going too slow on the benchmark? Should I cancel the training and start again with a harder benchmark? Or is this training going slow at the beginning and will go harder? I don't see how running 10 min + optional 10 min is going to help me run 21k / run for 2+ hours. I did my recent 10mi in about 1h45 and usually do a 10k in about an hour. I can understand that sometimes a short 10+10 min run (with 5+5 warmup/cooldown) is a good idea between challenging sessions, but here it got me 3-4 consecutive very short / easy sessions. submitted by /u/BenoitDuffez [link] [comments]
